What's new in Callout 0.8.1

Version 0.8.1 Alpha

0.8.1 adds one thing several of you asked for: rotation. A screenshot that arrived sideways — a phone capture, a scan — turns by 90° left, 90° right or 180° — left and right from the crop tool’s options column, all three from the Edit menu, with Preview’s shortcuts ⌘L and ⌘R. It is an edit like crop: everything you have drawn turns with the picture (text and stamps move but stay upright, because sideways text is never what anyone meant), ⌘Z reverses it, and because a quarter turn moves pixels without changing them, rotating back returns every one of them.

Nothing else changed. If you are reading this in the update window, that is the point: small things arrive as soon as they exist.

New

  • Rotate the Card. Left and right in the crop tool’s options; Edit has Rotate Left, Rotate Right and Rotate 180°, with ⌘L and ⌘R. The picture and your markup turn together; text and stamps stay upright; ⌘Z undoes it; rotating back is exact to the pixel.

What's new in Callout 0.8.0

Version 0.8.0 Alpha

0.8.0 is the first release that changes how Callout looks rather than what it does. Settings is now the standard Mac preferences window: a row of icons across the top — General, Capture, Appearance, Files, Updates — and the window sizes itself to the pane you are on. Nothing was removed or renamed; things moved to where you would look for them. The capture sound and the hotkeys are under Capture. The three update switches are under Updates, with a Check Now button beside them. General is back to five rows about the app itself.

And Show in the Dock, in General, now offers three choices: Always, as Callout worked before 0.7.8; Only while a window is open, as it works now and still the default; and Never — Callout lives in the menu bar and on its hotkeys, and its window opens without a Dock icon or a ⌘-Tab entry. Never is a real trade: with Callout’s window in front, the menu bar keeps showing the previous app’s menus, though Callout’s keyboard shortcuts all still work. The hint under the setting says so, so nobody picks it blind.

New

  • Settings, five panes. General · Capture · Appearance · Files · Updates, chosen from a toolbar; the window fits each pane. Every setting kept its name and its meaning.
  • Show in the Dock, three ways. Always · Only while a window is open (default) · Never. Never keeps the menu-bar icon and the hotkeys and opens the window without a Dock icon; the menu bar stays the previous app’s while Callout is in front.

What's new in Callout 0.7.8

Version 0.7.8 Alpha

0.7.8 changes one default, and it is the first thing to know: Callout now leaves the Dock when it has no window open. Close the window and the icon goes — it is still running, still in the menu bar, still on its hotkeys, and it comes straight back, Dock icon and all, the moment a Card lands or you open it from the menu bar. That is how Skitch and Shottr behave, and what several of you expected. If you would rather it always sat in the Dock, Settings → General → Show in the Dock has “Always”.

While Callout is out of the Dock it is also out of ⌘-Tab: the menu-bar icon and the hotkeys are the way back, which is how it was always meant to be used in the background. Starting at login in the menu bar now shows no icon at all until you need one. And updates now wait for you in the menu bar. Several of you said the hourly check was not working; it was, but the update window only ever appeared when you next came back to Callout, and if you worked all day by hotkey that could be never. Now a build found by the hourly check puts a small dot on the menu-bar icon and an “Update to…” item at the top of its menu; pick it and the update window comes to the front. It also appears by itself the next time Callout comes forward. Nothing interrupts you mid-sentence.

New

  • Out of the Dock when there is nothing to show. The Dock icon comes and goes with the window. Settings → General → Show in the Dock: Only while a window is open (the new default), or Always.
  • Updates wait in the menu bar. A build found by the hourly check is a dot on the menu-bar icon and an “Update to…” item at the top of its menu, and a badge on the Dock icon while there is one. It shows itself the next time Callout comes forward; it never interrupts what you are doing. The check when Callout launches is unchanged.
